text: The capacity of a muscle fiber to produce force is predicated on the position of the actin and myosin filaments in its sarcomeres. This phenomenon, known as the length-tension relationship (), can be harnessed to target muscles or portions of them by making them more or less active during exercise. Optimal force-producing capacity is often said to take place at approximately resting length, whereby the overlap of actin and myosin filaments is maximized, thus facilitating optimal crossbridge formation.
